MUQATIL:45:24-25/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:45:24-25/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:45:24-25/r1.claim: They think only worldly life exists: one generation dies and another is born from their descendants, so no one will be resurrected.

MUQATIL:45:24-25/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:45:24-25/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:45:24-25/r2.claim: They claim only the passage of time and alternation of night and day causes death; they have no knowledge and merely conjecture about resurrection.

FARRA:v3p47/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p47/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p47/r2.claim: Their claim نموت ونحيا means that they die and their descendants live after them; Arabic commonly attributes descendants' acts to their ancestors.

FARRA:v3p47/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p47/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p47/r3.claim: الدهر means the passage of long time, days, months, and years; Abdullah's reading دهر means a passing span of time.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p212#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p212#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p212#4/r1.claim: Qatada says Quraysh polytheists claimed that only worldly life exists and that time or age alone kills them.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p212#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p212#4/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p212#4/r2.claim: The Prophet forbids cursing time: God says He is time, turns night and day, and seizes people when He wills.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p405#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p405#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p405#5/r1.claim: Al-dahr means the passing of years and days.

TAB-FULL:v21p95/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p95/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p95/r1.claim: The polytheists deny any life beyond this worldly life, rejecting resurrection after death.

TAB-FULL:v21p95/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p95/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v21p95/r2.claim: Qatada says this was indeed the claim of the Arab polytheists.

TAB-FULL:v21p96/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r1.claim: They claim that passing nights and days and the length of a lifetime—not a Lord—cause their death and extinction.

TAB-FULL:v21p96/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r2.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r2.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh says, “Only passing time destroys us.”

TAB-FULL:v21p96/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r4.claim: Qatada says Quraysh polytheists claimed that only their lifetime destroys them.

TAB-FULL:v21p96/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r5.claim: The verse came because pagans blamed and cursed time for killing them; God says he, not time, causes their death and extinction.

TAB-FULL:v21p96/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r6.claim: The Prophet reports that pre-Islamic people blamed night and day for life and death and cursed time; God says he controls events and turns night and day.

TAB-FULL:v21p96/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r7.claim: A divine saying calls cursing time an offense against God, who holds command and turns night and day.

TAB-FULL:v21p96/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v21p96/r8.claim: Another report has God rebuke the servant who curses time by saying “woe to time,” while declaring that he is al-dahr.

TAB-FULL:v21p98#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p98#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p98#2/r1.claim: The polytheists have no certain knowledge or proof for their assertions about life and time; they merely conjecture and doubt, unsure of what they claim.

TAB-FULL:v21p98/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p98/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v21p98/r1.claim: The Prophet says no one should say “woe to time”: God turns night and day and can seize them when he wills.

TAB-FULL:v21p98/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p98/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v21p98/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra warns against cursing time, since God is the one who controls it.

ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r4.claim: One explanation of “we die and live” is that some people die while their children or another generation lives; this does not affirm resurrection.

ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r5.claim: A second explanation reverses no sequence: the coordinated verbs mean both dying and living, since waw does not show which comes first.

ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r6.claim: A third explanation is that humans began lifeless, then lived, and are finally destroyed by time.

ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p433/r7.claim: Their assertion that worldly life is all there is shows they deny resurrection; God identifies their claim as error and conjecture without knowledge.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3292/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3292/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3292/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra says the people of the pre-Islamic era attributed their destruction to night and day.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3292/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3292/r2.speaker: الله
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3292/r2.claim: The Prophet says God is harmed when people insult time, for command belongs to God, who turns night and day.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3292/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3292/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3292/r3.claim: Ibn Masud is reported reciting the verse about people who say they only live and die and time destroys them.

NAHHAS:v4p147/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p147/r12.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v4p147/r12.claim: He interprets the deniers’ claim as ‘we die and live,’ and rejects reversing the order to ‘live and die’; the author says Arabists allow word order to vary across the conjunction wāw.

NAHHAS:v4p147/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p147/r13.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p147/r13.claim: He glosses dahr as the long duration of passing days, nights, months, and years.

NAHHAS:v4p147/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p147/r14.speaker: قوم
NAHHAS:v4p147/r14.claim: One view says these people did not know God; if they had, they would know He causes death. Another says they knew God but blamed afflictions on natural causes and celestial motion without proof.

NAHHAS:v4p147/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p147/r15.speaker: قوم
NAHHAS:v4p147/r15.claim: A third view says these Arabs knew God, as shown by their claim that idols bring them near to Him, and some believed in resurrection.

THALABI:v8p363/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p363/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p363/r8.claim: The disbelievers say only worldly life exists: parents die, children live, and time or the length of life destroys people; the codex of Abd Allah adds that passing time destroys us.

THALABI:v8p364#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p364#2/r1.speaker: عمرو بن قميئة
THALABI:v8p364#2/r1.claim: Amr ibn Qumay'a's poem portrays time's daughters as shooting him with unseen misfortunes, leaving him barely able to stand.

THALABI:v8p364#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p364#2/r2.speaker: الشعبي
THALABI:v8p364#2/r2.claim: The report says al-Sha'bi recited verses to Abd al-Malik lamenting that time has taken their noble leaders and left them helpless.

THALABI:v8p364#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p364#2/r3.speaker: ابن لنكك
THALABI:v8p364#2/r3.claim: Ibn Lankak's poem accuses time of lowering generous people while elevating the base.

THALABI:v8p364#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p364#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v8p364#2/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda explains 'I am Time' to mean God brings and governs time's calamities, so cursing time's events in effect falls on God.

THALABI:v8p364#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p364#2/r5.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v8p364#2/r5.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl paraphrases the hadith as saying God is the maker of the ages.

THALABI:v8p364#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p364#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
THALABI:v8p364#2/r6.claim: Ibn Umar warns his son Salim against speaking of time, supporting the interpretation that time itself is not an independent agent.

THALABI:v8p364/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p364/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p364/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet explaining that pre-Islamic people blamed night and day for death and life, then God said that He is Time and turns night and day.

THALABI:v8p364/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p364/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
THALABI:v8p364/r2.claim: A report through Abu Hurayra says God forbids saying 'woe to time': He sends night and day and can seize them at will.

THALABI:v8p364/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p364/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p364/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's separate warning not to curse time because God is Time.

THALABI:v8p364/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p364/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام
THALABI:v8p364/r4.claim: Abu Ubayd begins explaining that Arabs blamed time for calamities and attributed events to it; the next segment supplies his interpretation of the hadith.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r1.claim: Their statement denies the Hereafter, resurrection, and recompense.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r10.speaker: الحسن عن النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r10.claim: He reports the Prophet forbidding time-cursing, since God controls the days.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r2.claim: The phrase is fronted and postponed: it means we live, then die; that is Ibn Masud's reading.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r3.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r3.claim: In the phrase as ordered, we die and our children live.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r5.claim: Dahr means lifespan or age; a poem speaks of time's strange changes.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r7.claim: He reports pre-Islamic Arabs said night and day alone destroy them and cause death and life; the verse responded.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r8.speaker: قطرب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p265/r8.claim: Dahr means death; a poem by Abu Dhuayb supports this.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r1.claim: The verse reports the deniers of resurrection saying that they have only worldly life and no later life.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r2.claim: Muqatil takes نموت ونحيا as generations dying while others born from their descendants live; the exegetes similarly understand one group dying as another lives.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r3.claim: Al-Farra says the descendants who come after them act as their parents did, a common Arabic attribution.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq gives two alternatives: the words mean we live and die, with no temporal order implied by واو; or people began as dead in origin and then lived.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r5.speaker: الكلبي والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi and the exegetes explain the claim about time as saying that only long life and the alternation of night and day destroy people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r6.claim: Qatada says they mean only the lifespan destroys us.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r7.speaker: ابن عيينة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r7.claim: Ibn Uyayna says the pre-Islamic Arabs thought time itself was what killed them and gave them life.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r8.claim: Their claim has no basis in knowledge; they speak from error and doubt, merely conjecturing rather than being certain.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p149#2/r9.claim: Muqatil glosses the final phrase as meaning that they do not know for certain, but speak conjecturally.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:45:23-25/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:45:23-25/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:45:23-25/r2.claim: The deniers claim this world is the only life: people die and their children live, and only the passage of time destroys them; they have no knowledge and merely conjecture.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r3.claim: Deniers say worldly life alone exists: parents die and children live; time, long life, and the alternation of night and day destroy them, without knowledge.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r4.claim: A divine report forbids saying “woe to time”: God is Time, sends night and day, and may seize them at will.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r5.claim: The Prophet forbids cursing time and calling grapes karm, saying God is Time and karm is the Muslim man.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p245#2/r6.claim: Arabs blamed time for calamities; because God is the real agent, cursing time ultimately curses God, so they were forbidden.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r1.claim: The words we die and live describe the human kind collectively: one group dies while another continues to live.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r2.claim: Their claim that time destroys them treats the long passage of time, in which afflictions unfold, as the killer; God says they have no knowledge and only conjecture.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads the claim as only a passing eon destroying them.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r4.claim: Mujāhid glosses dahr as time; Abū Hurayra reports that the pre-Islamic Arabs blamed night and day, while the Prophetic prohibition on reviling time means God causes what they attribute to time.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p87/r5.claim: The Prophet says not to revile time; in another report God says that the son of Adam abuses time, though God holds night and day in His hand.

TABRISI:45:22-24/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:45:22-24/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:45:22-24/r8.claim: Those denying resurrection say there is only worldly life, with no return or reckoning; their claim that time alone causes death reflects ignorance of the Creator and rests on conjecture.

TABRISI:45:22-24/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:45:22-24/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:45:22-24/r9.claim: The phrase we die and live may mean that the order is reversed, that people die and their children live, or that some die while others live.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p363/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p363/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p363/r1.claim: Dahr refers to the succession of night and day; the deniers have no knowledge and state this only as a conjecture.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p363/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p363/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p363/r2.claim: The Prophet said not to curse time, for God is the one who causes people to die, not the passage of time as they imagine.

RAZI-FULL:v27p232#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p232#2/r1.speaker: المشركون
RAZI-FULL:v27p232#2/r1.claim: The deniers of resurrection challenge the claim by demanding that their dead forefathers be brought back to testify that resurrection is real.

RAZI-FULL:v27p232#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p232#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p232#2/r2.claim: The challenge is weak: failure to occur now does not prove impossibility, just as our nonexistence before birth did not make our later existence impossible.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r1.speaker: أبو علي الثقفي
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r1.claim: His poem tells one who reproaches time that time is commanded and ends at God's command, contrasting the unbeliever's multiplying wealth with a poor believer's growing faith.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r10.claim: Some later Muslims who cannot publicly deny resurrection recast it as bodily death and afterlife rewards as images seen by souls; Qurtubi calls them more harmful than open disbelievers because they disguise truth and mislead.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes “we die and live” to mean that memories and traces survive, a life of remembrance.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r12.claim: A further view alludes to transmigration: when a person dies, the spirit enters inert matter and lives through it.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r2.claim: He rebukes his son Salim for speaking often of time and quotes a poem saying time neither perpetrates nor brings calamity; God raises an agent and reverses fortunes.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r3.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayd cites al-Aʿshā's poem: God retains fidelity and reckoning, while blame belongs to the person.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r4.speaker: عمرو بن قميئة
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r4.claim: His poem describes being struck by time's unseen arrows, illustrating how the Arabs attributed events to time.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r5.claim: The cited Prophetic report continues with God's statement that the son of Adam harms Him; the excerpt uses an ellipsis for the rest.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r6.claim: In debate with an atheist, Abū ʿUbayd argues that people did not curse God through all time; rather, Arabs blamed time for events, as al-Aʿshā's poem illustrates.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r7.claim: Arabs habitually blamed time during calamities and attributed events to it, although God alone is the true agent.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r8.claim: The phrase “they have no knowledge” uses min as an added particle; they say this from doubt and speak only by conjecture.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24#2/r9.claim: Among polytheists are people who acknowledge a creator but deny resurrection, and people who remain uncertain rather than rejecting it decisively.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r1.claim: The speakers deny the afterlife, resurrection, and recompense.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r10.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r10.claim: Quṭrub says only death destroys them and cites Abū Dhuʾayb's poem about fate and time.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r11.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r11.claim: ʿIkrima interprets “nothing destroys us but time” as “nothing destroys us but God.”

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r12.claim: The Prophet reports the pagan claim that night and day kill, followed by God's statement that He turns night and day and holds the affair; Qurtubi identifies the wording as Bukhari's, also transmitted by Muslim and Abū Dāwūd.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r13.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r13.claim: The Prophet also forbids saying “O woe to time,” since God is al-dahr; the report is in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r14.claim: Some scholars infer from the hadith that al-dahr is a divine name; others say it rebuts Arabs who treated time as an agent, since God causes the events they blame on time.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r2.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r2.claim: He reads “we die and live” as the parents dying while their children live.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r3.speaker: قراءة
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r3.claim: An alternate recitation vocalizes the nūn of naḥyā with ḍamma.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r4.claim: Another explanation is that some people die while others live.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r5.claim: His reading reverses the word order to “we live and die.”

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r6.claim: Mujāhid interprets al-dahr as the years and days.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r7.claim: Qatāda glosses al-dahr as a lifetime, equivalent in meaning to years and days.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r8.speaker: قراءة
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r8.claim: An alternate reading adds the wording dahr yamurr, time that passes.

QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r9.speaker: ابن عيينة
QURTUBI-FULL:45:24/r9.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna says the pagan Arabs thought time itself killed, gave life, and caused death; the verse came down about them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r1.claim: ما هي refers either to life itself or the present state; the speakers claim there is only this worldly life.

BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r2.claim: نموت ونحيا may describe humans as previously dead drops then alive, individuals dying while descendants live, alternating deaths and lives, or death and life with no afterlife; the words may also imply transmigration, held by many idolaters.

BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r3.claim: The claim that time alone destroys them attributes events independently to time and celestial motions; it may deny resurrection as well, or both claims, without knowledge or evidence.

BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:45:24/r4.claim: They merely conjecture, relying on inherited belief and rejecting what they have not perceived.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r1.claim: “We die and live” may mean parents die while their children live, some people die while others live, or lifeless semen becomes alive; it may also simply deny any life after worldly death.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r2.claim: Another view reads the statement as transmigration: a person dies and the soul then inhabits a lifeless body and lives there.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r3.claim: They claimed that days and nights cause death, denying the Angel of Death and God's command to seize souls, and blaming events on time.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r4.claim: The Prophet said not to curse time, for God—not time—is the bringer of events.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p133/r5.claim: Their claim rests on conjecture and guesswork, not knowledge or certainty.

QASHANI:45:23-24/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:45:23-24/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:45:23-24/r6.claim: Materialists reduce life to bodily death and sensory life, attributing both to time because they are veiled from the true agent who takes souls and grants life.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r10.claim: Dahr means the length of time in which calamities accumulate; if the speakers believe in God they wrongly attribute events to time, and if they deny God they are materialist Dahriyya attributing them to time.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r11.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r11.claim: Abdullah reads illa dahr, with an omitted verb understood as time passing; Arabs attributed every event to time and complained about it in poetry.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r7.claim: The denial that there is only worldly life is attributed to some Quraysh rejecting resurrection.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r8.claim: The apparent meaning of we die and live describes humanity collectively, one group dying and another living; another view reverses the sequence, and others take it to mean nonexistence followed by existence or parents followed by children.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r9.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p422/r9.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAli reads wa-naḥyā with a damma on the initial nūn.

SAMIN-DURR:45:24/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:45:24/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:45:24/r1.claim: The author notes that these verses have already been treated in a similar passage.

SAMIN-DURR:45:24/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:45:24/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:45:24/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads نحيا with ḍamma on the initial nūn.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p268#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p268#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p268#2/r1.claim: The deniers of resurrection say only worldly life exists and people alternate between dying and living. This includes Arab polytheists, philosophers who deny creation and return, and cyclical materialists who deny a Creator and posit endless 36,000-year repetitions.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p268#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p268#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p268#2/r2.claim: Their claim that time alone destroys them is unsupported conjecture; a sound divine report says God is the one who turns night and day, and people should not curse time.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p268#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p268#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p268#2/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says God is harmed by the human who curses time, since God controls the affair and turns night and day; another wording prohibits cursing time.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p269/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p269/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p269/r1.claim: Further reports from Abū Hurayra describe pre-Islamic people blaming night and day for death and life; a divine report says a human curses time while God controls night and day. Another report says God lent to a servant who refused and was insulted as 'time'.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p269/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p269/r2.speaker: الشافعي وأبو عبيدة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p269/r2.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Abū ʿUbayda, and other imams explain that Arabs blamed and cursed time for hardship, though God actually causes those events; cursing time therefore indirectly curses God. Ibn Kathīr calls this the best explanation.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p269/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p269/r3.speaker: ابن حزم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p269/r3.claim: Ibn Ḥazm and like-minded literalists wrongly count al-dahr as one of God's beautiful names based on this hadith.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r1.claim: The deniers claim worldly life is the only life, though “worldly” is a relative description that itself suggests another, later life.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r2.claim: Their saying “we die and live” means some people die and others are born; they deny that the same person lives after death and reduce themselves to animal-like attention to particulars.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r3.claim: They attribute their eventual destruction to time, which overcomes people through successive changes and unpleasant events; the author connects dahr to the verb meaning to overcome.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p105/r4.claim: They have no knowledge, only conjecture based on observing human decline with age and the fact that no dead person has returned.

DURR-FULL:v7p427/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p427/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p427/r1.claim: Ibn Masud's recitation says that worldly life is all there is: people die and live.

DURR-FULL:v7p427/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p427/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p427/r2.claim: In a divine report, God says that people harm Him by cursing time; He is time, holds command, and turns night and day.

DURR-FULL:v7p427/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p427/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p427/r4.claim: A divine report forbids saying that time has brought disappointment: God sends night and day and can seize them when He wills.

DURR-FULL:v7p427/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p427/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p427/r5.claim: Another divine report says God lent to a servant who did not repay, and the servant abused Him by saying alas, time, though God is time.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p190/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p190/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p190/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that people of the pre-Islamic era said only night and day destroy them, and the verse about attributing death to time was revealed.

BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r1.claim: The speakers are deniers of resurrection, identified as Quraysh and Arab polytheists; Kashf al-Asrar attributes the claim to heretics who called people like grass.

BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r2.claim: They say that life is only the present worldly life and that death and life recur here, with no existence beyond it; the word order may also serve the rhyme or simple coordination.

BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r3.claim: Some allow a transmigration reading: idol worshipers believed souls repeatedly transfer to new bodies after death; they attributed to a supposed prophet the claim of having seen 1,700 incarnations.

BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r4.claim: Al-Raghib defines transmigration’s proponents as rejecting the scriptural resurrection and believing souls pass eternally from one body to another.

BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r5.speaker: التعريفات
BURSEVI:v8p347#3/r5.claim: Al-Ta‘rifat defines transmigration as a soul attaching to another body immediately after leaving its former body, due to an innate affinity between soul and body.

BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r1.claim: Dahr means the passage of time or the world’s duration from its beginning to end, then any long period; zaman can denote either a short or long span.

BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r10.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r10.claim: A divine report says that when Adam’s child curses time, God is time: He sends night and day and can seize them whenever He wills.

BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r2.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r2.claim: Al-Qamus defines dahr as long time, extended eternity, or a thousand years.

BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r3.speaker: الصوفية
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r3.claim: Sufis define dahr as the enduring present, the extension of divine presence and hidden side of time, through which past and future are renewed.

BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r4.claim: The deniers blamed the passage of days and nights for death, rejecting the Angel of Death and his taking souls by God’s command.

BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r5.claim: The Prophet forbade cursing time: God, rather than time, brings events and is the true agent behind them.

BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r6.claim: Kashifi says the Exalted God turns the ages; time has no independent choice or agency in anything.

BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r7.claim: A poem warns against blaming time for betrayal: events obey a commanding Lord, while worldly abundance can increase a disbeliever’s unbelief and a believer’s faith despite poverty.

BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r8.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r8.claim: Al-Raghib explains the hadith to mean that God causes the good, evil, joy, and sorrow people attribute to time, so cursing time curses Him.

BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p347#4/r9.claim: Another interpretation takes the hadith’s second ‘dahr’ as an active participle: God is the manager and disposer of every occurrence; the author says the first reading is more apparent.

BURSEVI:v8p348/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p348/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p348/r1.claim: The first hadith’s meaning is readily understood in Sufi interpretation: God, not time, acts through the events people blame on time.

BURSEVI:v8p348/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p348/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p348/r2.claim: Their claim means that life is confined to this world and that life and death are attributed to time; they have no rational or transmitted knowledge for it.

BURSEVI:v8p348/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p348/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p348/r3.claim: They rely only on conjecture and imitation, whereas believers follow revealed texts with certainty and affirm both sensible and spiritual resurrection, the bridge, Paradise, and Hell.

BURSEVI:v8p348/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p348/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p348/r4.claim: Believers also affirm the gathering of individual souls with the universal soul and the union of intelligible and sensible realities, displaying divine power and perfection across unseen and visible realms.

BURSEVI:v8p348/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p348/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p348/r5.claim: This is the belief of prophets, messengers, and their believers; those who share it are saved, while others perish.

BURSEVI:v8p348/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p348/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p348/r6.claim: Tawhid requires attributing every event to God; the Prophet forbade cursing the wind because it is controlled by an angel under God, and all acts return to Him.

BURSEVI:v8p348/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p348/r7.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BURSEVI:v8p348/r7.claim: When summoned by al-Hajjaj, Anas said may God abase him, defining honor as obedience and disgrace as disobedience; he accused al-Hajjaj of opposing the Prophet’s way and humiliating God’s allies.

BURSEVI:v8p348/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p348/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BURSEVI:v8p348/r8.claim: When al-Hajjaj threatened to kill him, Anas said he would have worshiped him if he thought the power to kill belonged to al-Hajjaj, then began to cite a prayer taught by the Prophet.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r1.claim: The opening reports the outcome of their misguidance, sealing of hearing and hearts, and covering of sight; the pronoun can refer to the unbelievers or their state.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r10.speaker: الراغب، الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r10.claim: Al-Rāghib says dahr originally names the world's whole duration and then any long period; al-Khalīl records a use meaning that an affliction befell someone for a long time.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r11.claim: Blaming time for destruction denies the Angel of Death and attributes events to time through ignorance that God decrees them.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r12.claim: These speakers acknowledge God, unlike outright materialist Dahriyya, though both groups treat time as an independent cause; philosophers often measure time by celestial motion.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r13.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r13.claim: Muslim reports the prohibition on cursing time and the warning that God is the one who turns night and day.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r14.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r14.claim: Reports in Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, al-Ḥākim, and al-Bayhaqī prohibit cursing time; the cited divine speech says God turns night and day and brings events, so cursing time as agent falls on God.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r2.claim: The pronoun in mā hiya may mean life itself or the worldly state; either way the exception is from the same category.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r3.claim: Their statement generalizes about humankind: one group dies and another lives, with no resurrection; the order is chosen for the verse ending.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r4.claim: An alternate word order, “we live and die,” has been proposed, but al-Ālūsī says it is not convincing.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r5.claim: Another view takes death as the pre-ensoulment state before life begins.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r6.claim: Another reading uses life figuratively for the continuing descendants after their own deaths.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r7.claim: A further possibility assigns death and life to different people by figurative attribution.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r8.claim: Reading life as reincarnation into another body reflects a belief of many idolaters, but al-Ālūsī says it is unlikely here.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p152#3/r9.claim: Dahr means a long stretch of time and is narrower than zamān according to al-Saʿd; al-Rāghib describes it as the world's duration or any long period.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r1.claim: Some scholars count cursing time as a major sin because it can lead to cursing God; al-Ālūsī notes that Shāfiʿī legal language calls it disliked rather than forbidden or major.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r2.speaker: الشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r2.claim: The Shāfiʿī position is explicit that cursing time is disliked, not forbidden or a major sin.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī distinguishes meanings: cursing time itself is disliked; intending God or the true efficient cause is unbelief; an unqualified curse is ambiguous, though time is the apparent sense.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r4.claim: The claim that time-cursing is major when one believes time has causal power misses that this belief itself is unbelief, not merely a ruling about the curse.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r5.claim: Most scholars retain the nominative reading in the report “I am time”; it does not make time a divine name because the wording is figurative.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r6.claim: Some reject the nominative reading of the Abū Dāwūd and Ḥākim report as implying a divine name, and instead read time as an accusative adverb of duration.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r7.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib proposes that the second dahr in Muslim's report is a verbal noun meaning the active manager who directs events; al-Ālūsī considers this unlikely.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r8.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r8.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads “except time passes,” interpreting dahr as the time that elapses.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p153/r9.claim: Their assertion lacks rational or transmitted evidence and rests only on conjecture and imitation.

ELMALILI:45:22-26/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:45:22-26/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:45:22-26/r10.claim: The deniers have no knowledge for their claim about time’s power; they rely only on conjecture.

ELMALILI:45:22-26/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:45:22-26/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:45:22-26/r6.claim: The deniers claim earthly life is the only life: people die and live, and time alone destroys them; they deny any hereafter.

ELMALILI:45:22-26/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:45:22-26/r7.speaker: راغب
ELMALILI:45:22-26/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib defines dahr as the span from the world’s beginning to its end, but also as a long duration or a person’s lifetime; as a verb noun it can mean a calamity overtaking someone.

ELMALILI:45:22-26/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:45:22-26/r8.speaker: ابو حنيفة
ELMALILI:45:22-26/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa suspends judgment on how long an indefinite, unqualified use of dahr denotes.

ELMALILI:45:22-26/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:45:22-26/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:45:22-26/r9.claim: Time is broader than dahr, covering short and long past, present, and future intervals; here al-dahr means time’s passing or length because the destruction is partial, not the end of the world.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p357/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p357/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p357/r3.claim: The relative expression refers to mockers who assume life and death are confined to this world, as indicated by the following plural report of their speech.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r1.claim: This statement follows the argument in 45:21: their claim that their fate would be better was provocation, not belief in resurrection; their actual belief is that there is no life after death.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r2.claim: Hiyā may be the pronoun of the story, meaning the whole question of resurrection reduces to denying life after death; alternatively it refers elliptically to life, restricting life to this world.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r3.claim: ‘We die and live’ explains that no other world follows: some die while others remain or are born, and the present tense depicts recurring change; it cannot mean resurrection because the prior clause excludes it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r4.claim: The phrase may be their actual proverb or a Qur'anic concise rendering of ‘some die and others live’; waw does not imply chronological order.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r5.claim: Death is placed first to stress their claim that it ends life; it also creates the contrasts between worldly life and death, then death and life, with the cadence following that emphasis.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p361/r6.claim: The verse says they have no knowledge that time itself kills, since they offer no evidence for that claim.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r1.claim: By saying time alone destroys them, they confine life and death to this world: life comes through formation and death through the passage of time, aging, or destructive causes.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r2.speaker: عمرو بن قميئة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r2.claim: The old poet ʿAmr ibn Qumayʾa speaks of the daughters of time striking from where he cannot see, illustrating the personification of time as an agent.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r3.speaker: أسقف نجران
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r3.claim: The bishop of Najran likewise attributes impermanence to the sun's turning and rising, another poetic formulation about time and mortality.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r4.claim: Their conventional claim reflects little inquiry, despite their knowing God created the worlds; time is an abstract measure of intervals and seasons, so it cannot directly or indirectly cause death.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p362/r5.claim: The reference in ‘they have no knowledge of that’ is specifically their claim that time causes death; their basis is mere supposition or imaginative conjecture.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p363/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p363/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p363/r1.claim: The imperfect depicts belief as continually renewed and passed from elders to younger generations, which its adherents do not abandon.

TABATABAI:11:36-49#36/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:36-49#36/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:36-49#36/r3.claim: Arab paganism retained Sabian practices such as washing after sexual impurity and Brahmanic astrology; some also held the materialist view that time alone causes death.

TABATABAI:11:36-49#36/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:36-49#36/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:36-49#36/r4.claim: Some identify the claim that only worldly life exists and time destroys us with materialists who deny a creator.

TABATABAI:45:20-37#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:45:20-37#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:45:20-37#2/r1.claim: A Prophetic report says the agent behind the natural events people blame on time is God, so they should not curse the agent.

TABATABAI:45:20-37#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:45:20-37#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:45:20-37#2/r2.claim: In a divine report, God says not to curse time: He sends night and day and takes them when He wills.

TABATABAI:45:23-25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r2.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r2.claim: Dahr originally names the span of the world from its beginning to its end, and then any long duration; zaman can name short or long spans.

TABATABAI:45:23-25/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r3.claim: The context presents polytheists who accept a Creator but reject resurrection, not materialists who deny both origin and afterlife, who had not been mentioned.

TABATABAI:45:23-25/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r4.claim: They say there is no life beyond worldly life; some people die and others are born, maintaining the human lineage, while time gradually wears down all things.

TABATABAI:45:23-25/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r5.claim: The phrase about time destroying people denies transfer to another abode and resurrection; the author suggests this may be an ignorant Arab polytheist view.

TABATABAI:45:23-25/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r6.claim: Some exegetes read the statement as metempsychosis: souls leave bodies and enter new ones, enjoying or suffering according to their former deeds.

TABATABAI:45:23-25/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:45:23-25/r7.claim: Although possible, the transmigration reading poorly fits their attribution of destruction to time and their challenge to bring back their dead ancestors.

TABATABAI:45:24-27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:45:24-27/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:45:24-27/r1.claim: Other readings say people are dead before the soul enters and live afterward, or that dying and living refers metaphorically to descendants continuing the lineage.

TABATABAI:45:24-27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:45:24-27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:45:24-27/r2.claim: Their denial of resurrection is unsupported opinion: they have no evidence against it, while proofs establish its truth.

ASAD-NOTES:45:24#n26/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:45:24#n26/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:45:24#n26/r1.claim: The materialists' claim that time destroys them means death is accidental or caused by blind forces of nature.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p250/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p250/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p250/r4.claim: Verses 21–37 answer rejecters’ objections to the Hereafter, depict their condition there, and return to the theme of monotheism at the end.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r1.claim: The preceding verses argue for judgement from moral principles and evidence within and outside human beings; this verse presents the rejecters’ objection.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r2.claim: The rejecters say human existence is limited to worldly life: after death, everything ends.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r3.claim: They attribute death to time’s fortunes rather than God, comparing human lives to a tree that sprouts, matures, then withers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p271/r4.claim: God says their claim lacks knowledge and is speculation; they voice it to avoid limits on freedom and luxury.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r1.claim: The Hereafter follows from God’s power, wisdom, mercy, providence, and justice; without it creation would be purposeless amusement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r2.speaker: some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r2.claim: Some infer from the verse that a group of Arab atheists denied God and the Hereafter; Islahi rejects this as a group description.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r3.claim: Islahi says Arabs were polytheists, not a group of pure materialists: they doubted resurrection and expected their deities to secure rank and protect them from God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r4.claim: The time-fortunes claim does not deny God; Quraysh used it to counter the Qur’an’s warning that earlier peoples were destroyed for error, wrongdoing, and rejecting messengers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r5.claim: Quraysh’s alternative history portrayed nations as passing away through time regardless of beliefs or deeds, easing the warning that their own fate could match earlier peoples.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p272/r6.claim: Their philosophy is unsupported conjecture built to sanction desires; intellect, human nature, the world, prophets, and sages support the Qur’anic teaching.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p273/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p273/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p273/r1.claim: The passage closes with sorrow that people let conjecture guide them in a matter of such consequence.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r1.speaker: Bazı tefsirciler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r1.claim: Because the verse mentions dying before living, some exegetes infer that pre-Islamic Arabs believed in transmigration or reincarnation.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r2.claim: Although initially plausible, the reincarnation reading lacks historical evidence that Arabs held such a belief.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r3.claim: The verse instead explains that idolaters deny resurrection in another life and that this denial underlies some of their harmful conduct.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:45:24/r4.claim: Other verses clarify that “we die and live” means denying resurrection, not believing in reincarnation.

STUDYQURAN:45:24/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r1.claim: The statement that this world is all there is expresses disbelievers' rejection of Resurrection.

STUDYQURAN:45:24/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r10.claim: Their claim about what follows worldly life has no basis; the text's language about conjecture is compared with 53:28 and 49:12.

STUDYQURAN:45:24/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r2.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r2.claim: One reading of “we die and live” allows only one life and one death, with no afterlife.

STUDYQURAN:45:24/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r3.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r3.claim: Other readings mean that some people die while others live, or that parents die while their children live.

STUDYQURAN:45:24/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r4.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r4.claim: In pre-Islamic Arabia, people commonly cursed the passage of time when hardship struck.

STUDYQURAN:45:24/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r5.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r5.claim: The Prophet forbade cursing time and transmitted God's saying that Adam's son vexes Him by doing so, for God controls affairs and alternates night and day.

STUDYQURAN:45:24/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r6.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r6.claim: The alternation of life and eventual death attributed to time is actually caused by God.

STUDYQURAN:45:24/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r7.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r7.claim: Cursing time for one's suffering effectively curses God, the Agent behind everything that happens.

STUDYQURAN:45:24/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r8.claim: Failure to see time's passage as a sign of God's omnipotence and the meeting with Him results from failure to reflect on God's signs.

STUDYQURAN:45:24/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:45:24/r9.speaker: author

STUDYQURAN:45:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:45:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:45:intro/r10.claim: The rest of the sūrah focuses on deniers of God's signs, the Final Judgment, and the peril awaiting them on that Day.
